_comment: Bridge profiles describe WHERE four routing fields sit inside another app's QR payload.
They never describe what any other field means, and the Bridge never parses one.
THE PROFILES IN THIS FILE MUST BE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE. When two profiles fit one payload,
detection refuses it — it does not pick a winner, because 'verified' means a profile's
indices are right for payloads FROM THAT APP and says nothing about whether this payload
came from it. Preferring a verified generic profile over an app-specific one routes real
payloads through wrong indices, silently, invisible until picklist night.
The three profiles below are fully specified by this project and are disambiguated by
format (JSON vs delimited) and by match format (bare number vs full TBA match key).
`npm test` asserts the set is unambiguous against a corpus of payloads.
App-specific profiles are NOT shipped active. See UNVERIFIED-examples.json.

profiles.name: Generic tab-separated
profiles.notes: Field order is scout, match number, team, then any number of app-defined columns that Courier carries through untouched. Tab only: there is no quoting, so a delimiter that can occur inside a value would shift every column.

profiles.name: Generic tab-separated, full match keys
profiles.notes: As the generic TSV profile, but the match column carries a full TBA-style key (2027mose_sf1m2) so elimination matches can be ingested. The event key embedded in that match key is checked against the Bridge's configured event.

profiles.name: Generic JSON object
profiles.notes: Any additional keys are carried through untouched. Routing fields may be addressed with a dotted path ("meta.team") or, when a key legitimately contains a dot, with exact segments (["meta", "team.number"]).
